title: Numbers: 1 to 5
summary: Reach up to 1 through 5 with the finger that owns each column, since it is the same finger you already use.

explain.goal: Type 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 with the correct fingers.
why: The number row is just one more row above the top row. You use the same finger as the keys below it, reaching one row further.
That is why the map works: every column has one finger, whether the key is a letter or a number.
how: Left pinky: 1. Left ring finger: 2. Left middle finger: 3.
Reach up with the finger, press, and return to home.

mistakes.mistake: Reaching for a number with a different finger
mistakes.reason: Each number sits in a column with its own finger. Sticking to it is easier than remembering exceptions.
The number row is a long reach, and moving the hand loses your home position.

explain.recap: Numbers follow the same columns as the letters below them. Same finger, one row further.

title: Numbers: 6 to 0
summary: Reach 6 through 0 on the right side, using the same fingers that own those columns.

explain.goal: Type 6, 7, 8, 9, and 0 with the correct fingers.
why: The right side of the number row follows the same rule as the left. Each number is typed by the finger that owns its column.
This is where your right index finger's second column shows up: it owns both 6 and 7.
how: Right index finger: 6 and 7. Right middle finger: 8. Right ring finger: 9.

mistakes.reason: 0 sits in the pinky's column. Keeping to the map means you never have to think about it.
The long reach makes mistakes easy. Accuracy first, speed later.

explain.recap: Right hand numbers: 6 and 7 for the index finger, then 8, 9, and 0 for the middle, ring, and pinky fingers.

title: Numbers: Mixed
summary: Mix all the number keys together, so the number row feels as familiar as the letters.

explain.goal: Type mixed numbers with the correct finger every time.
why: Real numbers jump around the number row, so you have to know each key's finger without stopping to think.
This is practice for that recall, and the same finger map keeps it predictable.
how: Use the finger that owns each number's column, and return to home after each reach.
Keep your eyes on the text.

mistakes.mistake: Looking at the keyboard for each digit
mistakes.reason: You would lose the rhythm you have been building. The columns are in your hands by now.

mistakes.mistake: Hitting the row below instead of the number
mistakes.reason: A missed reach types a letter. Reach fully up before pressing.

explain.recap: Numbers are just one more row. Use the same finger for the column and return home.
